sara_ml: Quick bring-up note — ran nebula-lite-10b on int6 vs int8 yesterday. Wanted a short triage before we pick routing. TL;DR: int6 cheaper (~2.8x token-cost vs int8) but shows a small regression on our QA metric for long-context summarization slices (~3.7% absolute). p50 latency is great, p95 moves up ~40ms on int6 for >1024 tokens.

mike_prod: Can you drop the topline unit-econ numbers? product needs to know expected per-request delta.

sara_ml: Sure — baseline (nebula-lite-10b int8): cost = $0.0095 per 1k tokens, p50=85ms, p95=210ms, QA score=82.1. int6: cost = $0.0034 per 1k tokens, p50=78ms, p95=250ms, QA score=78.4. These are synthetic slice-weighted averages from user-like traces.

joel_platform: Nice cost delta. What's the failure/hallucination signal look like? Any catastrophic cases?
\

tina_eval: On the long-dialog slice (avg len 1400 tokens) int6 increases hallucination/repetition flags — precision@1 drops (~4.1%) and a small bump in factuality alerts. Short-turn chats are basically equal.

mike_prod: So product tradeoff is ~3.7% QA hit weighted by long-context usage. Do we have an estimate of how much of traffic is long-context?

sara_ml: From our traffic sample: ~19% of requests exceed 1k tokens, but only ~7% exceed 1.5k. If we weight by token consumption, the long-context group accounts for ~31% of token-volume.

joel_platform: Suggestion: hybrid routing with context-aware policy. Serve int6 for short (<1024) by default, and route >1024 to int8. Could further soften with sampling.

mike_prod: Is it worth a fraction-of-traffic canary on int6 for long-context too (to measure real user impact) or do we block long-context int6 entirely?

sara_ml: My recommendation: default routing = int6 for <1024; for 1024-2048 run canary = 15% int6 / 85% int8; for >2048 stick to int8 for now. That captures most unit-econ wins without exposing too many long-context users.

joel_platform: I can express that as a rollout rule. Proposed policy snippet:

```
{
  "route_rules": [
    {"max_tokens":1024, "model":"nebula-lite-10b-int6", "traffic_pct":100},
    {"min_tokens":1025, "max_tokens":2048, "model_pool":[{"model":"nebula-lite-10b-int8","pct":85},{"model":"nebula-lite-10b-int6","pct":15}]},
    {"min_tokens":2049, "model":"nebula-lite-10b-int8", "traffic_pct":100}
  ]
}
```

deploy-bot: deploy plan created: canary=15% for slice 1025-2048, start_time=3344556700, monitor=latency+QA+hallucination.

mike_prod: For GTN/metrics we need clear thresholds to abort. Propose: if QA delta vs baseline >2.5% (weighted) OR hallucination alerts increase >30% OR p95 latency increase >20% then auto-rollback. ok?

tina_eval: Agree. Also add a manual check after 12 hours for failures not captured by our heuristics — I'll run a 1k-sample qualitative pass at 24h.

joel_platform: I'll wire the metrics in Console dashboards: per-route QA, hallucination_rate, cost_per_token, and per-route token-volume. Also add a trace hook so we can inspect KV-cache usage for int6 — saw a couple of degraded cache-hit cases in the microbench logs.

sara_ml: One more econ note: at our current traffic profile the hybrid plan yields ~28% platform token-cost reduction vs all int8, with estimated savings ~$12k/month at current spend. Net estimated product impact (based on traffic weighting + QA delta) ~ -0.6% weighted QA (within acceptable).

mike_prod: Sounds reasonable — proceed with canary and the thresholds. Can we spike the canary to 30% for the first 2 hours to get signal faster, then drop to 15%?

joel_platform: We can. I'll schedule: start at 30% for 2 hours, then 15% for 46 hours, then escalate or rollback. Doc the schedule in the runbook.

deploy-bot: canary rollout started at 3344556700 — monitoring hooks active. :rocket:

tina_eval: I'll post the 24h qualitative readout in this thread. For now, early sample looks ok but slightly more generic phrasing on long summaries — not catastrophic.

sara_ml: Thanks all. If we see any hallucination alerts spike, we'll divert traffic to opt13b-int8 fallback and pause the roll.

mike_prod: Thank you team. Follow-ups: joel to add dashboard, tina to do 24h QC, sara to prepare prompt tweaks if needed. :thumbsup:
